We’re in the heart of the UK government with direct lines to No. 10 (the Prime Minister's office), and we work with frontier developers and governments globally.</p> <p>We’re here because governments are critical for advanced AI going well, and UK AISI is uniquely positioned to mobilise them. With our resources, unique agility and international influence, this is the best place to shape both AI development and government action.</p></div><div class="vac_display_field"> <div class="vac_display_field_value"> <div class="vac_display_field"> <div class="vac_display_field_value"> <h2><strong>The deadline for applying to this role is 11th October 2026, end of day, anywhere on Earth. </strong></h2> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p></p> <p class="text-node">AI capabilities in cybersecurity and autonomy are advancing faster than at any point in history. Frontier models can now work through multi-step network intrusions, discover and exploit software vulnerabilities, and carry out long-horizon technical tasks with increasing independence. These are extraordinary tools for scientific and economic progress, but also have the potential for serious harm if misused or deployed without adequate oversight, as seen in the recent cybersecurity incidents.<br><br>The team evaluates the capability of both frontier and open-weight AI models in cybersecurity, autonomy and AI R&amp;D, ensuring the UK government and its partners have an accurate view of risks and capabilities. description:
<p>Hudson River Trading (HRT) is looking for a Data Production Engineer to join our Data team. Data is at the core of everything we do at HRT; we excel at deriving deep insights from all types of data, allowing us to achieve consistent success in a dynamic market.&nbsp;</p> <p>This role is an opportunity to work directly with live trading teams to support one of the largest automated trading systems in the world. You will write automation, explore data, work closely with our research and trading teams, and interact with a variety of external partners such as data providers, brokers, and exchanges. In addition to being a critical part of the trading process, you will have the opportunity to acquire, analyze, and prepare data for quantitative research.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Data Engineering: Write tools to classify, onboard, and reconcile data. Onboard datasets, explore data, and automate tasks using a modern Python data stack</li> <li>Data Analysis: Parse, analyze, and understand data sets. description: <div class="content-intro"><h2>About the AI Security Institute</h2> <p>The AI Security Institute is the world's largest and best-funded team dedicated to understanding advanced AI risks and translating that knowledge into action. We’re in the heart of the UK government with direct lines to No. 10 (the Prime Minister's office), and we work with frontier developers and governments globally.</p> <p>We’re here because governments are critical for advanced AI going well, and UK AISI is uniquely positioned to mobilise them. With our resources, unique agility and international influence, this is the best place to shape both AI development and government action.</p></div><div class="vac_display_field"> <div class="vac_display_field_value"> <div class="vac_display_field"> <div class="vac_display_field_value"> <h2><strong></strong></h2> <h2><strong>The deadline for applying to this role is 11th October 2026, end of day, anywhere on Earth. &nbsp;</strong></h2> <h2><strong><br>About the team</strong> </h2> <p></p> <p class="text-node">AI capabilities in cybersecurity and autonomy are advancing faster than at any point in history. Frontier models can now work through multi-step network intrusions, discover and exploit software vulnerabilities, and carry out long-horizon technical tasks with increasing independence. These are extraordinary tools for scientific and economic progress, but also have the potential for serious harm if misused or deployed without adequate oversight, as seen in the recent cybersecurity incidents.</p> <p class="text-node">Our Cyber &amp; Autonomous Systems Team evaluates the capability of both frontier and open-weight AI models in cybersecurity, autonomy and AI R&amp;D, ensuring the UK government and its partners have an accurate view of risks and capabilities. We use realistic cyber ranges and a large CTF suite for our evaluations, run pre-deployment testing of frontier models, and collaborate with our partners across UK government, frontier labs, and NCSC.</p> <h2><strong>Role Description</strong></h2> <p><strong></strong></p> <p class="text-node"></p> <p class="text-node">We are looking for exceptional Software Engineers at all experience levels, from junior through to senior or staff, who want to work at the forefront of frontier AI security</p> <p class="text-node">In this role, you’ll work with cutting-edge technologies on research problems with real-world impact, and receive mentorship and coaching from your manager and the technical leads on your team.</p> <p class="text-node">Your day-to-day work might include building state-of-the-art evaluations (e.g., <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.11214" target="_blank">cyber ranges</a>), running pre-deployment testing exercises (e.g., <a href="https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/our-evaluation-of-claude-mythos-previews-cyber-capabilities" target="_blank">Claude Mythos Preview</a>), validating novel model behaviours (e.g., <a href="https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/cheating-behaviour-in-frontier-model-evaluations" target="_blank">models cheating in evaluations</a>), and answering timely research questions (e.g., <a href="https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/how-far-behind-the-frontier-are-leading-open-weight-models-on-cyber" target="_blank">the capabilities of open-weight models</a>). You would be working alongside engineers and researchers who care deeply about the impact of their work, take pride in their craft, and have a high level of autonomy.</p> <p class="text-node">If that sounds exciting to you, we'd love for you to apply!</p> <h2 class="text-node"><strong>Core Responsibilities</strong></h2> <p><strong></strong></p> </div> </div> </div> </div> <div class="vac_display_field"> <div class="vac_display_field_value"> <ul> <li><strong>Build evaluation infrastructure</strong>: develop systems and code that make cyber and autonomy evaluations possible at scale.</li> <li><strong>Develop analysis tooling:</strong> turn raw results into insights, including LLM-as-a-judge and other analysis workflows.</li> <li><strong>Lead testing exercises:</strong> identify key research questions, run evaluations to collect evidence, analyse results, and communicate findings and recommendations.</li> <li><strong>Deliver engineering work:</strong> own technical projects and shared components from design through implementation, iteration, and maintenance.</li> <li><strong>Write production-quality code:</strong> build scalable, robust, maintainable Python software with strong testing, documentation, and observability practices.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Example projects</strong></h3> <ul> <li><strong>Onboard a cyber range:</strong> deploy a new cyber range on AISI’s evaluation infrastructure (for example, Proxmox) and verify it meets the internal Evaluation Quality Standard.</li> <li><strong>Build an image pipeline:</strong> create a pipeline that converts infrastructure-as-code into AMIs ready for evaluation.</li> <li><strong>Develop a more secure sandbox service:</strong> partner with Core Technology to improve AISI’s sandbox platform, representing CAST to ensure the service meets its evaluation requirements.</li> <li><strong>Prepare data for publication:</strong> collect, validate, and organise evaluation data to support publication of research findings.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Impact</strong></h2> <p>Your work will directly shape the UK government's understanding of AI cyber capabilities, inform safety standards for frontier AI systems, and contribute to the global effort to develop rigorous evaluation methodologies. The evaluations you build will help determine how advanced AI systems are assessed before deployment.</p> <h2><strong>Who we're looking for</strong></h2> <p>We're flexible on the exact profile and expect successful candidates will meet many (but not necessarily all) of the criteria below:</p> <h3><strong>Essential&nbsp;</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Delivering and maintaining production-quality software</li> <li>Deep Python experience, with a clear view of what good Python looks like and broad familiarity with the wider ecosystem and tooling</li> <li>Designing and evolving software systems or technical architecture</li> <li>Strong interest in helping to improve the safety of AI systems</li> <li>Take ownership of ambiguous, technically hard problems and follow through</li> <li>Communicate clearly and raise engineering standards through feedback and mentoring</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Desirable</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Cybersecurity or adversarial-security expertise</li> <li>Building, operating, or analysing AI evaluations</li> <li>Experience building, deploying, and operating production systems using DevOps practices</li> <li>Familiarity with AI misuse and loss-of-control threat models</li> </ul> <p>Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if you don't meet all the above criteria.</p> </div> </div><div description: About Agicap Créée à Lyon en 2016 par trois entrepreneurs français, Agicap est l'une des scale-ups avec la plus forte croissance d’Europe, avec plus de 8 000 clients, 600 employés et une croissance rapide du chiffre d'affaires (multiplié par 7 entre 2021 et 2024). Agicap fait partie du French Tech 120, qui récompense les startups les plus prometteuses de France. Agicap permet aux directions financières des entreprises de taille intermédiaire de gérer et de prévoir efficacement leur trésorerie, de payer leurs fournisseurs et de se faire payer. En combinant un système de gestion de trésorerie avec des solutions de gestion des comptes fournisseurs et des comptes clients sur une seule plateforme, Agicap ambitionne de devenir la nouvelle référence en matière de gestion de trésorerie pour les entreprises de taille intermédiaire. Nous avons levé 145 millions d’euros depuis notre création, auprès de fonds de capital-risque prestigieux tels qu’AVP, Greenoaks, Partech et BlackFin, avec un dernier tour en novembre 2024. Ces ressources supplémentaires alimentent encore davantage notre innovation produit, nous permettant de croître significativement et d’accélérer notre expansion internationale à travers le monde. Nous sommes convaincus que notre succès réside dans nos équipes passionnées et dévouées, engagées à bâtir une entreprise où chacun peut évoluer et construire sa carrière. Nous sommes constamment à la recherche de nouveaux talents, visant l’excellence et prêts à rejoindre notre aventure ambitieuse ! Agicap est en train de devenir une AI-first company . Nous formons l'ensemble de nos employés à travailler avec l'IA et à automatiser eux-mêmes une partie de leurs tâches. Certains projets sont trop longs, trop transverses ou trop techniques pour être portés par une équipe métier seule. C'est le rôle de l'AI Lab. C'est l'équipe pivot qui construit les outils internes qui changent la façon dont Agicap travaille au quotidien. Notre boussole : impact opérationnel rapide , itérations courtes, travail à 360° avec toutes les équipes (Sales, CS, Finance, Produit, Marketing, Data, C-level). C'est une création de poste : l'accélération de l'IA change nos process et notre manière de bosser. On a besoin d'un renfort senior pour accompagner cette transition et l'inscrire dans des pratiques qui tiennent sur le long terme. L'équipe que tu vas rejoindre :  3 personnes , toi inclus : un ingénieur IA junior , un Tech Lead à mi-temps (qui sera ton manager), un Product Manager . Ton rôle : apporter le recul technique qui manque aujourd'hui dans l'équipe (infra, architecture, maintenabilité, scalabilité) — construire vite, mais sans creuser de dette pour demain. Tu es en interaction directe avec toutes les équipes métier d'Agicap : c'est un poste très transverse, très exposé. ⚡️ Responsabilités : Tu alternes entre cadrage rapide, build et itération : Comprendre le besoin d'une équipe métier en direct, cadrer ce qui a réellement de l'impact vs. ce qui est du confort, prioriser. Construire les outils internes de bout en bout : cadrage → dev → mise en prod → itération avec les utilisateurs. Faire évoluer la plateforme IA commune : serveurs MCP, intégrations, outillage transverse mis à disposition de toute l'entreprise. Prendre les décisions techniques qui structurent le Lab : infra, choix de stack, architecture. Il n'y a pas d'existant lourd auquel te conformer, tu construis pour scaler. Élever le niveau technique de l'équipe : mentoring de l'IA Engineer junior, transmission des bonnes pratiques, revue de code utile. Identifier proactivement les process où l'IA apporte un vrai gain — et construire la solution. Exemples de chantiers sur tes 6 premiers mois : Feedback loop produit : construire un système qui digère l'ensemble des logs de feedback client (calls, RFP, remontées CS) et produit des recommandations priorisées pour les Product Managers. Aujourd'hui la donnée existe mais on ne la digère pas. Chantier infra MCP : mettre à disposition des collaborateurs Agicap des serveurs MCP connectés à leurs outils du quotidien, à l'échelle. ⚡️Comment on travaille : Autonomie totale : équipe de 3, tu décides, tu assumes tes choix. Ship rate élevé : on livre quotidiennement, on mesure, on itère. Pas de sprints à la papa. Full remote ou hybride Lyon/Paris, comme tu préfères. Venues à Lyon possibles (~1 fois toutes les 6 semaines) mais jamais obligatoires . IA au quotidien dans le delivery : on utilise Claude, OpenAI, Mistral au quotidien pour construire — on n'observe pas la vague IA, on est dedans. Anglais requis : beaucoup de collaborateurs sont anglophones. Ton binôme est francophone. 👀 Le profil recherché: On vise un profil senior avec expérience de Tech Lead — quelqu'un qui a déjà pris des décisions impactantes, poussé des sujets techniques exigeants, et exploré activement le terrain IA : ~4-5 ans d'expérience minimum en dev, sur des projets réellement mis en production. Expérience de Tech Lead ou équivalent : tu as déjà driver des décisions d'architecture et d'infra, tu sais arbitrer entre vélocité et dette. Pratique concrète et récente des LLMs : tu as essayé des choses, poussé des expérimentations, testé Claude / OpenAI / Mistral. Tu es moteur sur ces sujets, pas suiveur. Python et TypeScript dans ta boîte à outils. Le langage compte moins que ta capacité à choisir le bon outil pour le bon problème. Bases techniques solides : tu maîtrises et comprends ce que tu livres. Capacité à livrer vite et à prioriser ce qui a réellement de l'impact — mode Doer, pas mode powerpoint. Proactivité et curiosité : tu identifies des opportunités que personne n'a formulées, tu vas chercher. Anglais professionnel courant. Autonomie assumée : dans une équipe de 3, tu ne peux pas te cacher.  ⭐ Stack et outillage LLMs : Claude (Anthropic), OpenAI, Mistral — l'équipe n'est pas mono-provider, tu choisis le bon modèle pour le bon usage. Outillage IA en interne : serveurs MCP, plateforme IA commune, agents connectés aux outils métier. title: CENTRALE LYON - Post Doctoral Open and Flexible System-Level Evaluation Framework for Emerging AI Computing Architectures
description: Emerging computing technologies – non-volatile and ferroelectric memories, analog and digital in-memory computing, silicon photonics, 3D integration, and heterogeneous chiplets – offer major gains in energy efficiency, latency, bandwidth, and functionality. Their potential cannot, however, be established from device or circuit results alone: it requires a rigorous link between technology characteristics, architectural choices, workload mapping, and application-level figures of merit. The Electronics group at the Lyon Institute of Nanotechnology (INL) is seeking a (m/f) postdoctoral researcher to develop an open, modular and extensible system-level evaluation framework for design space exploration (DSE) and system-design-technology co-optimization (SDTCO) of emerging computing architectures. The focus is at the interface of computer architecture, accelerator design, performance modelling and hardware-software codesign, while making systematic use of lower-level device, circuit and array results so that architectural conclusions remain physically credible. The objective is to convert low-level results – compact models, measured or simulated KPIs, variability and reliability constraints, and multi-objective Pareto fronts – into parameterized architectural models supporting efficient exploration of accelerators for emerging AI workloads. The framework must enable both bottom-up projection, from device/circuit/array choices toward system performance, and top-down constraint propagation, from targets for energy, latency, throughput, accuracy, robustness and area toward technology and circuit requirements. It will consolidate ongoing INL activities in predictive system assessment, DTCO, emerging memories, compute-in-memory and photonic computing, integrating or extending existing components with emphasis on openness, reproducibility and reusability. A core scientific challenge is to represent cross-layer trade-offs without hiding their origin: rather than isolated energy or latency numbers, the framework should expose bottlenecks, sensitivities, feasibility limits, break-even points and opportunities and identify the regimes in which a technology becomes advantageous. Target workloads span edge inference through to transformer-inspired models, with use cases in vision, audio and sensor processing, sparse and vector/matrix operations, and on-device learning. Expected outcomes: a maintainable evaluation environment combining fast exploration with selected higherfidelity validation paths; cross-layer models and interface contracts, reusable data schemes, benchmarking flows, system-level Pareto analyses and design guidelines for emerging AI accelerators – a decision-support instrument for future research projects. Candidate profile: PhD in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related discipline, with a strong background in several of: computer architecture and AI accelerators; performance, energy and area modelling; design space exploration and multi-objective optimization; hardwaresoftware co-design and workload mapping; emerging memories, compute-in-memory or photonic computing. Strong Python skills and sound software-engineering practice are essential; experience with SystemC, C/C++, RISCV simulation, QEMU, PyTorch/ONNX workload flows, architecture simulators (NeuroSim, CiMLoop/AccelForge, Timeloop or similar) will be appreciated. Familiarity with circuit-level modelling or EDA is an asset, but the focus is architectural and system-level research. Environment: the position is hosted by the Electronics group at INL (UMR CNRS 5270), Ecole Centrale de Lyon, Écully, France – an interdisciplinary environment spanning devices, circuits, architectures, design automation, photonics and integrated systems, with national and European collaborations. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.</p> <p>Our 5 values guide how we collaborate:</p> <ul> <li>💡<strong> Work Hard Together:</strong> Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success</li> <li>🏆 <strong>Get Things Done: </strong>&nbsp;We prioritize action and efficiency for impactful results</li> <li>🚀 <strong>Go Above &amp; Beyond:</strong>&nbsp; We tackle challenges proactively and always aim for excellence</li> <li>🎓 <strong>Succeed Through Expertise:</strong> Knowledge sharing and continuous learning are core to our culture</li> <li>🤝 <strong>Satisfy &amp; Empower Clients:</strong> We're committed to our clients' success</li> </ul></div><div class="s-whitespace-pre-wrap s-break-words s-font-normal first:s-pt-0 last:s-pb-0 s-py-1 @md:s-pt-2 @md:s-pb-[10px] @md:s-leading-relaxed s-text-base s-leading-relaxed s-text-foreground dark:s-text-foreground-night"> <h2 class="s-whitespace-pre-wrap s-break-words s-font-normal first:s-pt-0 last:s-pb-0 s-py-1 @md:s-pt-2 @md:s-pb-[10px] @md:s-leading-relaxed s-text-base s-leading-relaxed s-text-foreground dark:s-text-foreground-night">The Team You Will Join&nbsp;</h2> <div class="s-whitespace-pre-wrap s-break-words s-font-normal first:s-pt-0 last:s-pb-0 s-py-1 @md:s-pt-2 @md:s-pb-[10px] @md:s-leading-relaxed s-text-base s-leading-relaxed s-text-foreground dark:s-text-foreground-night">&nbsp;</div> <div class="s-whitespace-pre-wrap s-break-words s-font-normal first:s-pt-0 last:s-pb-0 s-py-1 @md:s-pt-2 @md:s-pb-[10px] @md:s-leading-relaxed s-text-base s-leading-relaxed s-text-foreground dark:s-text-foreground-night">You'll be part of our Executive Assistant team led by <strong class="s-font-semibold s-text-foreground dark:s-text-foreground-night">Claire, Executive Assistant to the CEO</strong>.
